extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, researchers, commenters, and developers who use FederalRegister.gov
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using FederalRegister.gov: searching and saving documents, understanding public inspection, submitting formal comments, drafting and researching Federal Register documents, and using developer APIs. Covers site-specific procedures, accessibility, and resources for document drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of Site Feedback and email addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Our “Site Feedback” tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues. The Office of the Federal Register (OFR) and GPO have no authority or ability to process comments on rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting formal comments on rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov supports submitting formal comments on documents without leaving the site via a “Submit a Formal Comment” feature developed with Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the site’s 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature (or Regulations.gov where applicable) to submit comments on rulemaking documents; do not use site-feedback channels for policy comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Inspection page purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue and may include documents scheduled for later issues at an agency's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Public Inspection page to access important or complex documents before their official publication in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document text feature — activation of agency-included links
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, FederalRegister.gov activates those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website no longer exists. The site also provides automated legal links where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document utility bar and sidebar features
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents include a utility bar (sidebar) that provides quick access to the Public Inspection version, the official electronic format of the published document, printing, and sharing tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the icons on the utility bar to access alternate document formats, the Public Inspection version, and to print or share documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tools and citation search
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov provides a basic search box and an advanced document search. You can search by citation (for example, '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the basic search for general queries and the advanced options when you need targeted searches or to search by specific citation formats; the 'Search' navigation pull-down shows search options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving documents for later (MyFR clippings)
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov allows users to save documents for later use via a MyFR feature named 'clippings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents can be clipped from a document’s page or from search results by clicking the flag icon; a MyFR account is required to manage clippings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting and research resources to follow
rubrics_metrics.description: The site links to resources to help understand document drafting and research, including the Drafting Document Drafting Handbook, Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook, Federal Register Bulletins, and Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing Federal Register documents, consult these official resources and plain-language tools (Federal Register Plain Language Tools, PlainLanguage.gov), the Thesaurus of Indexing Terms, and the List of Subjects by CFR Title to align with OFR expectations and improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and drafting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: OFR provides guidance and tools (including Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act and Plain Language Tools) to support plain-language drafting of Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting should follow plain-language principles and OFR/GPO drafting handbooks to improve public accessibility and comprehension of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility compliance and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is designed following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines; it uses text-based files and PDFs that are text-accessible through Adobe PDF Tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR and GPO are committed to assisting people with disabilities; see the Accessibility page for details and contact information for access support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer resources and REST API data provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register data originate with the files used to produce the print and PDF editions; during publication these are transformed into bulk XML files and MODS metadata files. The site provides a REST API and interactive documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers can use the REST API and client libraries (including an official Ruby API client gem) to access Federal Register data; review API docs and GitHub repositories for usage patterns and data structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source availability of FederalRegister.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is a fully open source project and its source code is available on GitHub in multiple repositories (for example, federalregister-api-core).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the public repositories to understand how the site imports data, serves API responses, and to contribute or build client tooling; note repositories may be under active maintenance or cleanup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and citation patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: The site documents various patterns for linking to FederalRegister.gov and explains different convenient citation formats for Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing Federal Register documents externally, follow the linking and citation patterns explained on the site to ensure stable and correct references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact channels for different issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information is provided for editorial content questions (fedreg.info@nara.gov), programming and technical issues (support ticket), and accessibility inquiries (Accessibility page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate contact channel depending on whether your issue is editorial, technical/programming, or accessibility to get the correct assistance.
